title: Structured output: graceful fallback, truncation safety, escaping and retry modes
creator: Ava Patel
description: Design and implement a robust strategy for streaming structured JSON outputs that handles mid-stream truncation, in-flight escaping edge cases (unclosed braces, embedded binary/base64 content, nested tool-call frames), and clear retry semantics compatible with older clients. The deliverable is a backwards-compatible protocol extension and server/runtime changes plus tests and docs. This ticket focuses on the policy/spec and runtime guardrails; implementation will land across runtime and SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Spec document published in Confluence with examples for all common edge cases
Runtime implements framing and partial-envelope behavior behind a feature flag
SDKs (JS + Python) can detect partial responses and either resume or surface a clear partial-object error to callers
Integration tests simulate truncation mid-object and validate client/server recovery or deterministic fallback
No regression in existing streaming boolean tests and latency SLOs remain within 5% for small messages
implementation_notes: When a chunk ends with an unbalanced JSON bracket, runtime should not attempt best-effort repair; instead mark envelope.status=partial and emit a stable resume_token computed from KV-cache offset and request id
For embedded binary or user-supplied blobs: recommend base64 encoding in the model output or use a secondary artifact stream (artifact URL) to avoid breaking JSON streaming

Backfill a backward-compatible header negotiation: clients that do not understand ENVELOPE-v1 will continue to receive previous newline-delimited partial token stream; runtime will map token stream to envelope on the server side where possible

Retry semantics: clients may retry by resending the same request with header 'X-Resume-Token: <resume_token>'. Server will accept resume tokens within a TTL window (default 30s) and replay KV-cache deltas to continue generation. If resume token is stale, server returns 412 + structured error with 'non_resumable' and a recommended fallback (complete the best-effort JSON with 'partial:true' envelope and close).
Idempotency: resume is only allowed for requests with deterministic seed or explicit idempotency key provided; otherwise runtime must refuse resume with guidance to restart full generation
Compatibility layer: expose a runtime flag 'compat.envelope_to_tokens' that converts new envelope frames into the legacy token stream for older clients during a migration window
Observability: emit metrics for 'partial_emits', 'resume_attempts', 'resume_success', 'resume_fail_stale' and log the last-balanced-offset for debugging
Performance trade-offs: small additional header bytes per chunk; handshake adds a tiny RTT on first event but reduces client complexity and expensive re-parsing on retries

Failure mode: if client cannot resume and parser sees final stream is invalid JSON, SDK should return a structured 'PartialOutputError' containing the 'envelope' meta and the last well-formed prefix as a string

decisions: Decision: use explicit ENVELOPE-v1 header per event for structured streaming instead of wholesale switching to length-prefixed binary frames — reason: maximum compatibility with text-first clients and easier human debugging
Decision: resume token must be HMAC'd and TTL-limited (30s default) to avoid long-lived replay vectors; store minimal state to enable replay (KV-cache delta + model rand seed)
Decision: do not auto-rewrite malformed JSON server-side; treat as signal of truncation and surface partial envelope to client for deterministic retry
Decision: implement a compatibility conversion mode in runtime to translate envelope into legacy token stream to avoid breaking older SDKs during rollout
review_feedback: PM note (Jordan Lee): ensure UX for developers is explicit — SDKs should expose both 'resume' and 'fallbackToPartial' helpers
Security (Ria Kumar): resume tokens must be HMAC using per-tenant key and rotated; include guidelines in security checklist
SDK lead (Mei Chen): JS SDK should expose a streaming parser that yields 'Envelope' objects; keep binary size impact < 3KB
Infra (Omar Haddad): store ephemeral resume state in redis cluster with 5s replication window; provide metrics for eviction rates
test_plan: Unit: envelope encode/decode fuzz tests including nested braces, escaped quotes, embedded '\n' and long binary payloads
Integration: simulate mid-stream termination at offsets 1..N and validate resume logic and TTL expiry behavior
E2E: exercise a real client (JS + Python) hitting hosted runtime with feature flag off/on and assert identical final JSON for non-truncated flows
Chaos: randomly drop last 50-200 bytes to validate SDK partial error surfaces and docs examples
open_questions: TTL: should default be 30s or 2 minutes for high-latency regions? (trade-off: longer TTL increases attack surface and memory pressure)
Resume determinism: how do we verify model determinism across transient kernel changes? (proposal: only allow resume for seeded/deterministic requests)
Migration: what's the safe rollout percentage for turning on envelope_for_all? suggested ramp: 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 2 weeks
SDK ergonomics: prefer 'resume()' method on stream object or a higher-level 'completeOrResume()' helper?
